# check-opencloud-security

check-opencloud-security is an independent service that runs a built-in
scanner against a public OpenCloud instance. It measures version support,
known advisories, TLS, headers, hardening, and exposed services. The service
queues scans and keeps each result for a short, configured retention window.
The developer of this tool is Massoud Ahmed.

## Discovery and contracts

- `GET /llms.txt`: this overview.
- `GET /.well-known/ai.json`: machine discovery for the API, workflows, and
  Model Context Protocol endpoint.
- `GET /openapi.json`: OpenAPI 3.1 operations and schemas.
- `GET /arazzo.json`: asynchronous scan, polling, export, and erasure
  workflows.
- `POST /mcp`: server-side MCP tools when enabled.

## Main HTTP operations

- `POST /api/scans`: queue one scan. Send `target_url`,
  `ignore_hardenings`, `release_track`, and `output_format` only.
- `POST /api/scans/batch`: queue several targets under the same options.
- `GET /api/scans/{uuid}`: poll a scan and read its structured result.
- `GET /api/scans/{uuid}/export/{format}`: export `json`, `csv`, `sarif`, or
  `pdf`.
- `DELETE /api/purge?target=...`: operator-authorized erasure, when enabled.

Release tracks are `auto`, `rolling`, `production`, and `lts`. Waivers hide
an alert from the rating but keep the evidence in the result. A scan UUID is
the whole authorization for that scan. Do not publish it, guess UUIDs, or
retry a 404.

## Browser WebMCP

When MCP is enabled, pages with useful actions register tools through WebMCP.
The landing page offers `scan_opencloud_security`. A result page offers
`get_scan_result` and `export_scan_report`. Their JSON Schemas contain the
options available on the rendered page. Tool execution calls the same HTTP
API listed above with `Accept: application/json`; it does not bypass SSRF
checks, rate limits, target cooldowns, queueing, or result isolation.

Use the page-scoped WebMCP tools when running inside a supporting browser.
For a remote agent, start with `/.well-known/ai.json`, use `/mcp` when
available, or follow the OpenAPI and Arazzo documents. A `202` means the scan
was queued. Poll the UUID until `done` is true. A `409` from export means the
scan exists but is not finished; a `404` is final.

WebMCP draft: https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/
